title: Models cheat with watermarks, rulers and backgrounds
body: Classifiers have learned to detect horses from a photographer's watermark, skin lesions from the ruler beside them, and huskies from snow. Geirhos and colleagues named it shortcut learning: networks take the easiest predictive feature, intended or not. Accuracy on a test set drawn from the same shortcuts certifies the cheating, which is why out-of-distribution tests exist.
source_hint: Geirhos et al., Nature Machine Intelligence (2020)
